To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of aerosol mixtures of pollen grains with background aerosol leads to an increase in the depolarization and spectral dependence of the depolarized backscattering ratio.
multiwavelength Mie-Raman-Fluorecence lidar can be used to detect pollen grains in aerosols and to distinguish them from background aerosols.
simultaneous measurements of depolarization ratio and fluorescence allow to identify aerosol mixtures with pollen grains and to separate dust, biomass burning particles and mixtures with pollen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of pollen grains on optical properties of aerosol mixture in the north of Europe.
the development of the new lidar technique for the detection of the pollen grains in atmospheric aerosol mixture and for the characterization of their optical properties.
the development of a new approach to the identification of aerosols in the atmosphere based on the measurements of the depolarizing ratio and fluorescence backscattering coefficient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lidar observations of the aerosol depolarization ratio at 355 and 532 nm and fluorescence backscattering coefficient at 466 nm are very promising for the discrimination of aerosol mixtures and identification of pollen grains in the atmospheric boundary layer.
the Mie–Ramon–fluorescence measurements are a very useful tool for the detection of the aerosols containing the pollen grains, especially during the pollen season.
the multiwavelength lidar technique is very promising for aerosol monitoring and for the study of the aerosol optical properties in the presence of pollen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lidar observations of the aerosol depolarization ratio and fluorescence are useful for the detection of the presence of pollen in aerosol mixture.
the lidar observations of the aerosol depolarization ratio together with fluorescence backscattering can be used for aerosol identification during the pollen season.
the lidar measurements are a powerful tool for the study of the atmosphere, and the Mie-Raman-Fluorosence technique is a good way for aerosol characterization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the depolarization measurements at 355, 532 and 1064 nm combined with fluorescence measurements at 466 and 607 nm can provide a powerful tool for aerosol characterization and identification of pollen grains in the aerosol mixtures.
the depolarization and depolarization ratio spectral dependence are useful for aerosol identification and classification.
Mie–Ramon–fluorescence measurements are a promising tool for the study of aerosol mixtures and their impact on climate.
